summary: Gone 1930s wooden L-4 cab on Pompey Peak, Gifford Pinchot NF, WA; Aircraft Warning post 1942-43; burned 1958; a 2021 note says the trailhead road washed out.

facts.design: Wooden L-4 cab, 10 ft per FFLOS; one side on the summit rocks and the other on a lower level (Willhite)
facts.status_note: Burned in 1958; a 1961 USGS party found the lookout house and other buildings burned

staffing.status: Aircraft Warning Service post, activated November 8, 1942 and deactivated October 15, 1943

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

access.note: Trail 128 is open to hikers, horses and bicycles and closed to motorized use. A 2021 Forest Service note says the trailhead road has been washed out; Willhite describes a drivable approach on Forest Road 20.

visit.trail_note: Willhite's route: Forest Road 20 for roughly 13 miles, then the Klickitat Trail and Pompey Peak Trail from the east, a 9.5-mile round trip. The Forest Service says the trail is reached from Klickitat Trail #7 or from Forest Road 20 at Jackpot Lake.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service says 1934; FFLOS and firelookout.com say the 1930s; Willhite says likely the early 1930s. The story uses the 1934 date from the Forest Service and does not claim it is certain.

Willhite describes Forest Road 20 as drivable for any vehicle with potholes and one washout. A Forest Service note dated 10/4/2021 says the trailhead has been inaccessible for 10 years because of road washouts. The story gives both and asks readers to call the ranger district first.
The Forest Service says the peak was named for a pack mule that died in the 1890s. Willhite calls that story questionable because the name appears on a 1915 map. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief kind (two_story) matches Willhite's cab-on-two-levels description; FFLOS calls it a 10-ft L-4 tower, so the 10 ft may be the cab height rather than total height, and no height_m is recorded. The brief's access 'unknown' is replaced by public because the trail is open, but the trailhead road is disputed: the Forest Service note is dated 10/4/2021 on a page last updated June 16, 2025, so confirm with the Cowlitz Valley Ranger District before publishing. Willhite's visit date is not given; his photo captions mention 2019. A 1956 newspaper item names an observer; the name is left out. Burn and abandonment dates agree across sources.
